page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard3.64 is a dedicated bare metal server built on the x86_64 architecture, powered by Intel Xeon 8358 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The server configuration supplies 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs via multithreading at 2 threads per core. System memory totals 1024 GB, which translates to a density of 8 GB of RAM per vCPU or 16 GB per physical core.

As a bare metal offering, compute and memory allocations are fully dedicated to the tenant without virtualization or hypervisor overhead. The hardware profile does not include local NVMe storage or discrete GPU accelerators, meaning operational file systems and persistent storage must be attached via remote block storage networks. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio positions the server for memory-intensive enterprise tasks. Suitable workloads include large relational and in-memory database engines, enterprise resource planning platforms, high-throughput batch processing pipelines, and dense private virtualization hosts.
